title: L002: Add LocalReporter and MultiReporter with credentials
description:
**Size:** 🏗️ large
**Category:** backend
**Priority:** critical
**Source:** Proposed for 'It should be possible in Metrics, Log Forwarding u'

Implement per-pipeline `LocalReporter` (metrics, logfwd, auditfwd) — an HTTP client implementing the respective reporter interface that POSTs identical JSON batch payloads (MetricBatch/LogBatch/AuditBatch) to the configured local URL with bearer token authentication. Implement per-pipeline `MultiReporter` fan-out wrapper that dispatches to both platform reporter and local reporter in parallel goroutines, collecting and logging errors independently (local endpoint failure never blocks platform delivery). Credential resolution at flush time via existing `SecretFetcher.FetchSecret()` → `DecryptSecret()` (AES-256-GCM) with an in-memory TTL cache to avoid per-flush secret lookups. Includes comprehensive unit tests: LocalReporter HTTP behavior, MultiReporter parallel dispatch, credential caching TTL expiry, error isolation between targets.

**Rationale:** Core business logic of the feature. The MultiReporter pattern ensures zero impact on existing platform delivery while enabling local endpoint support. In-memory credential caching avoids expensive secret decryption on every flush cycle. Independent error handling is critical — a down local SIEM must never cause data loss to the platform.

**Affected Areas:**
- src/internal/metrics/local_reporter.go
- src/internal/metrics/multi_reporter.go
- src/internal/logfwd/local_reporter.go
- src/internal/logfwd/multi_reporter.go
- src/internal/auditfwd/local_reporter.go
- src/internal/auditfwd/multi_reporter.go
- src/internal/metrics/local_reporter_test.go
- src/internal/metrics/multi_reporter_test.go
- src/internal/logfwd/local_reporter_test.go
- src/internal/logfwd/multi_reporter_test.go
- src/internal/auditfwd/local_reporter_test.go

stories.title: Platform operator delivers metrics to a local SIEM endpoint
stories.want: to configure a local HTTPS endpoint so that metrics are delivered to both the Plexsphere platform and my local SIEM in parallel
stories.so_that: I can ingest metrics into my own monitoring stack without disrupting platform telemetry
criteria: When local_endpoint.url is set in metrics config, MetricBatch payloads are POSTed to the local URL in addition to the platform
The local HTTP POST uses Content-Type: application/json and includes an Authorization: Bearer header with the resolved secret
Platform delivery succeeds even when the local endpoint is unreachable
When local_endpoint.url is empty, behavior is identical to the existing single-reporter pipeline

stories.title: Platform operator delivers logs to a local SIEM endpoint
stories.want: to configure a local HTTPS endpoint so that forwarded logs are delivered to both the platform and my local log aggregator in parallel
stories.so_that: I can search and analyze logs in my own tooling alongside platform log forwarding
criteria: When local_endpoint.url is set in logfwd config, LogBatch payloads are POSTed to the local URL in addition to the platform
The local HTTP POST body is identical JSON to what the platform receives
Log forwarding to the platform is unaffected by local endpoint availability
Local endpoint errors are logged with component=logfwd but not propagated to the forwarder

stories.title: Platform operator delivers audit events to a local SIEM endpoint
stories.want: to configure a local HTTPS endpoint so that audit events are delivered to both the platform and my local audit store in parallel
stories.so_that: I can maintain a local copy of audit trails for compliance requirements
criteria: When local_endpoint.url is set in auditfwd config, AuditBatch payloads are POSTed to the local URL in addition to the platform
Subject and Object json.RawMessage fields are preserved unchanged in the local POST body
Audit forwarding to the platform continues normally even if the local endpoint returns errors
The audit forwarder's Status() method still reflects platform-level error counts, not local

stories.title: Local SIEM is unreachable but platform delivery continues
stories.want: platform telemetry delivery to be completely unaffected when my local SIEM is down or slow
stories.so_that: a misconfigured or failing local endpoint never causes data loss to the Plexsphere platform
criteria: MultiReporter dispatches to platform and local reporter in parallel goroutines
Platform reporter error is returned to the pipeline manager (preserving existing retry/retain semantics)
Local reporter error is logged as a warning but not returned to the pipeline manager
A slow local endpoint (hanging HTTP request) does not delay platform delivery or block the flush cycle

stories.title: Credential resolution caches bearer token with TTL
stories.want: to resolve the local endpoint bearer token via SecretFetcher and cache it in memory with a TTL
stories.so_that: per-flush secret lookups and AES-256-GCM decryption are avoided while still supporting secret rotation
criteria: On first Report call, LocalReporter fetches the secret via SecretFetcher.FetchSecret() and decrypts via DecryptSecret()
Subsequent Report calls within the TTL window reuse the cached plaintext token
After TTL expiry, the next Report call triggers a fresh FetchSecret+DecryptSecret cycle
If credential fetch fails but a stale cached token exists, the stale token is used and a warning is logged

stories.title: No local endpoint configured — existing behavior preserved
stories.want: no behavioral change when I have not configured a local endpoint
stories.so_that: upgrading to this version has zero impact on existing deployments
criteria: When LocalEndpoint.URL is empty, the pipeline manager receives the ControlPlane client directly (no MultiReporter wrapping)
No additional goroutines are spawned for local reporting
No SecretFetcher calls are made for credential resolution
Pipeline startup logs do not mention local endpoint when not configured

stories.title: TLS configuration respected for local endpoint
stories.want: to control TLS certificate verification for the local endpoint independently
stories.so_that: I can connect to internal endpoints with self-signed certificates during initial setup
criteria: When tls_insecure_skip_verify is false (default), TLS certificate verification is enforced
When tls_insecure_skip_verify is true, certificate verification is skipped for the local endpoint only
The platform ControlPlane client's TLS settings are never affected by local endpoint TLS config
LocalReporter creates its own http.Client with the configured TLS settings

requirements.description: LocalReporter SHALL POST the identical JSON batch payload to the configured local HTTPS URL
requirements.rationale: The local endpoint receives the same data format as the platform, enabling consistent ingestion without payload transformation

scenarios.name: Successful POST to local endpoint
scenarios.when: LocalReporter.Report*(ctx, nodeID, batch) is called with a valid batch
scenarios.then: an HTTP POST is made to the configured URL with the batch JSON-serialized as the request body
and_then: Content-Type header is application/json
HTTP method is POST
request body deserializes to the same batch type

scenarios.name: Local endpoint returns non-2xx status
scenarios.when: the local endpoint responds with HTTP 500
scenarios.then: LocalReporter returns an error describing the status code
and_then: the error includes the HTTP status code
no retry is attempted within the same Report call

scenarios.name: Local endpoint is unreachable
scenarios.when: the local endpoint URL cannot be connected to (connection refused, DNS failure)
scenarios.then: LocalReporter returns a connection error
and_then: the error wraps the underlying net/http error

requirements.description: LocalReporter SHALL include the resolved bearer token in the Authorization header of every request
requirements.rationale: Bearer token authentication is the only supported auth mechanism for local endpoints, ensuring secure access

scenarios.name: Authorization header present on POST
scenarios.when: LocalReporter makes an HTTP POST to the local endpoint
scenarios.then: the request includes an Authorization header with value 'Bearer {resolved_token}'
and_then: the token is the plaintext result of DecryptSecret, not the ciphertext or secret key name

scenarios.name: Credential resolution failure — no cached token
scenarios.when: credential resolution fails and no cached token is available
scenarios.then: LocalReporter returns an error and does not make the HTTP POST
and_then: no request is sent to the local endpoint without authentication

scenarios.name: Credential resolution failure — stale cached token available
scenarios.when: credential resolution fails but a previously cached token exists (expired TTL)
scenarios.then: LocalReporter uses the stale cached token and logs a warning
and_then: the HTTP POST is still attempted with the stale token
a warning log includes the fetch error

requirements.description: Credential resolution SHALL use the existing SecretFetcher.FetchSecret() → DecryptSecret() pipeline
requirements.rationale: Reuses the established encrypted secret delivery mechanism without introducing a parallel credential flow

scenarios.name: First credential resolution
scenarios.when: LocalReporter resolves credentials for the first time
scenarios.then: it calls SecretFetcher.FetchSecret(ctx, nodeID, secretKey) then DecryptSecret(nsk, ciphertext, nonce)
and_then: the resolved plaintext is stored as the bearer token
the cache timestamp is set to now

scenarios.name: DecryptSecret returns error
scenarios.when: FetchSecret succeeds but DecryptSecret returns an error (corrupt ciphertext, wrong NSK)
scenarios.then: credential resolution fails with a wrapped error
and_then: no partial state is cached
the error message does not leak cryptographic details

scenarios.name: FetchSecret returns error
scenarios.when: FetchSecret returns a network or API error
scenarios.then: credential resolution fails with a wrapped error
and_then: the caller can distinguish fetch failure from decrypt failure via error wrapping

requirements.description: LocalReporter SHALL cache the resolved bearer token in memory with a TTL of 5 minutes
requirements.rationale: Avoids expensive per-flush SecretFetcher calls and AES-256-GCM decryption while supporting credential rotation within a bounded window

scenarios.name: Cache hit within TTL
scenarios.when: Report* is called within 5 minutes of the last successful credential resolution
scenarios.then: the cached token is used without calling SecretFetcher
and_then: no FetchSecret or DecryptSecret calls are made

scenarios.name: Cache miss after TTL expiry
scenarios.when: Report* is called more than 5 minutes after the last successful credential resolution
scenarios.then: a new FetchSecret+DecryptSecret cycle is triggered
and_then: the cache is updated with the new token and timestamp

scenarios.name: Concurrent Report calls share cache
scenarios.when: multiple goroutines call Report* simultaneously while the cache is valid
scenarios.then: all goroutines read the same cached token without data races
and_then: sync.RWMutex protects cache access

requirements.description: MultiReporter SHALL dispatch to platform reporter and local reporter in parallel goroutines
requirements.rationale: Parallel dispatch ensures that a slow local endpoint does not delay platform delivery

scenarios.name: Both targets succeed
scenarios.when: both platform and local reporter return nil error
scenarios.then: MultiReporter returns nil error
and_then: both reporters received the same nodeID and batch arguments

scenarios.name: Slow local endpoint does not delay platform
scenarios.when: the local reporter takes 5 seconds to respond while the platform reporter responds instantly
scenarios.then: the platform reporter's result is available immediately (not blocked by local)
and_then: MultiReporter waits for both to complete before returning

scenarios.name: Context cancellation propagated to both
scenarios.when: the context is cancelled while both reporters are in-flight
scenarios.then: both reporters receive the cancelled context
and_then: MultiReporter returns the platform reporter's error (context.Canceled)

requirements.description: MultiReporter SHALL return only the platform reporter's error; local reporter errors SHALL be logged independently
requirements.rationale: The pipeline manager's retry/retain logic must only respond to platform delivery failures; local endpoint failures are informational

scenarios.name: Platform succeeds, local fails
scenarios.when: platform reporter returns nil but local reporter returns an error
scenarios.then: MultiReporter returns nil (success)
and_then: the local error is logged as a warning with the component name

scenarios.name: Platform fails, local succeeds
scenarios.when: platform reporter returns an error but local reporter returns nil
scenarios.then: MultiReporter returns the platform error
and_then: the pipeline manager retains the batch for retry (existing behavior)

scenarios.name: Both fail
scenarios.when: both platform and local reporter return errors
scenarios.then: MultiReporter returns the platform error only
and_then: the local error is logged as a warning
the platform error triggers the pipeline's retry/retain logic

requirements.description: LocalReporter SHALL create its own http.Client with TLS settings from LocalEndpointConfig
requirements.rationale: The local endpoint's TLS configuration (including skip-verify) must be independent of the platform client's TLS settings

scenarios.name: Default TLS verification
scenarios.when: TLSInsecureSkipVerify is false
scenarios.then: the HTTP client verifies the server's TLS certificate against system roots
and_then: connections to endpoints with invalid certificates fail with a TLS error

scenarios.name: Skip TLS verification
scenarios.when: TLSInsecureSkipVerify is true
scenarios.then: the HTTP client skips certificate verification
and_then: connections to endpoints with self-signed certificates succeed

scenarios.name: Reasonable request timeout
scenarios.when: the local endpoint is unresponsive
scenarios.then: the HTTP client times out after a reasonable duration (e.g., 10 seconds)
and_then: the timeout error is returned to the caller

requirements.description: Pipeline wiring SHALL only create MultiReporter when LocalEndpoint.URL is non-empty
requirements.rationale: Zero-impact on existing deployments that do not configure a local endpoint

scenarios.name: Local endpoint configured
scenarios.when: cfg.<pipeline>.LocalEndpoint.URL is non-empty at startup
scenarios.then: a LocalReporter and MultiReporter are constructed, and the MultiReporter is passed to the pipeline manager as the reporter
and_then: startup log indicates local endpoint is enabled with the target URL

scenarios.name: Local endpoint not configured
scenarios.when: cfg.<pipeline>.LocalEndpoint.URL is empty (default)
scenarios.then: the ControlPlane client is passed directly to the pipeline manager (no wrapping)
and_then: no LocalReporter or MultiReporter is instantiated
no startup log about local endpoint

scenarios.name: All three pipelines wired independently
scenarios.when: only metrics has a local endpoint configured (logfwd and auditfwd do not)
scenarios.then: only the metrics pipeline uses a MultiReporter; logfwd and auditfwd use the ControlPlane client directly
and_then: each pipeline's local endpoint configuration is independent

requirements.description: LocalReporter SHALL use a dedicated HTTP request timeout of 10 seconds
requirements.rationale: Prevents a hanging local endpoint from consuming resources indefinitely; shorter than the platform client's 30s timeout since local endpoints are expected to be on the same network

scenarios.name: Request completes within timeout
scenarios.when: the local endpoint responds within 10 seconds
scenarios.then: the response is processed normally

scenarios.name: Request exceeds timeout
scenarios.when: the local endpoint does not respond within 10 seconds
scenarios.then: the HTTP client cancels the request and returns a timeout error
and_then: the error is returned to the caller (MultiReporter logs it)

scenarios.name: Context deadline shorter than timeout
scenarios.when: the parent context has a deadline of 3 seconds
scenarios.then: the request is cancelled at 3 seconds (context deadline takes precedence)

requirements.description: LocalReporter credential resolution SHALL NOT log or expose the plaintext bearer token
requirements.rationale: Security requirement: bearer tokens are sensitive credentials that must not appear in logs, error messages, or debug output

scenarios.name: Successful credential resolution
scenarios.when: credential resolution succeeds
scenarios.then: no log entry contains the plaintext token value
and_then: log entries may reference the secret key name but not the resolved value

scenarios.name: Credential resolution failure
scenarios.when: credential resolution fails
scenarios.then: the error message does not contain any ciphertext, nonce, or token fragments
and_then: error messages use generic phrasing like 'credential resolution failed'

scenarios.name: Stale token fallback
scenarios.when: stale token is used after TTL expiry
scenarios.then: the warning log mentions 'using cached credential' without revealing the token value

tasks.title: Implement metrics LocalReporter with HTTP POST, bearer auth, credential caching, and unit tests (REQ-001, REQ-002, REQ-003, REQ-004, REQ-007, REQ-009, REQ-010)
tasks.description: Create `internal/metrics/local_reporter.go`: struct implementing MetricsReporter interface with fields for http.Client, URL, SecretFetcher, NSK, secretKey, logger, and cached credential (token string + fetchedAt time.Time protected by sync.RWMutex). Constructor `NewLocalReporter(cfg api.LocalEndpointConfig, fetcher SecretFetcher, nsk []byte, nodeID string, logger *slog.Logger) *LocalReporter` creates http.Client with TLS config from cfg.TLSInsecureSkipVerify and 10s timeout. `ReportMetrics(ctx, nodeID, batch)` resolves credential (check cache TTL 5min, fetch+decrypt if expired, fallback to stale on error), then POSTs JSON-serialized batch to cfg.URL with Authorization: Bearer header. Define `SecretFetcher` interface in this package (matching nodeapi pattern). Create `internal/metrics/local_reporter_test.go`: tests using httptest.NewTLSServer for HTTP behavior (correct method, path, Content-Type, Authorization header, request body), credential caching (second call within TTL doesn't call fetcher), credential refresh (call after TTL triggers fetcher), stale fallback (fetch error with cached token uses stale), no-cache error (fetch error with no cache returns error), non-2xx handling, connection error handling. Use mock SecretFetcher returning pre-encrypted test secrets.

tasks.title: Implement metrics MultiReporter with parallel dispatch, error isolation, and unit tests (REQ-005, REQ-006)
tasks.description: Create `internal/metrics/multi_reporter.go`: struct implementing MetricsReporter with fields for platform MetricsReporter, local MetricsReporter, and logger. Constructor `NewMultiReporter(platform, local MetricsReporter, logger *slog.Logger) *MultiReporter`. `ReportMetrics(ctx, nodeID, batch)` launches two goroutines (one for platform, one for local), waits for both via sync.WaitGroup, returns platform error only, logs local error as warning with component=metrics. Create `internal/metrics/multi_reporter_test.go`: tests using mock reporters for both-succeed, platform-fail-local-succeed (returns platform error), platform-succeed-local-fail (returns nil, logs warning), both-fail (returns platform error, logs local warning), slow-local-doesn't-block-platform (verify timing), context-cancellation-propagated, both-receive-same-arguments.

tasks.title: Wire MultiReporter into up.go for all three pipelines when LocalEndpoint.URL is non-empty (REQ-008)
tasks.description: Modify `cmd/plexd/cmd/up.go`: For each pipeline (metrics, logfwd, auditfwd), add conditional wrapping. Before the pipeline manager constructor, check if `cfg.<Pipeline>.LocalEndpoint.URL != ""`. If set: construct LocalReporter with (cfg.LocalEndpoint, client (as SecretFetcher), nsk, identity.NodeID, logger), then construct MultiReporter wrapping (client, localReporter, logger), pass MultiReporter as the reporter argument. If not set: pass client directly (existing behavior). Log info message when local endpoint is enabled: 'local endpoint enabled' with url field. Ensure NSK ([]byte(identity.NodeSecretKey)) is available before pipeline construction. The ControlPlane client implements SecretFetcher (has FetchSecret method), so it can be passed directly.

tasks.title: Credential cache edge case tests: TTL boundary, concurrent access, stale fallback under load (REQ-004, REQ-010)
tasks.description: Add edge case tests to `internal/metrics/local_reporter_test.go` (representative for all three pipelines): (1) TTL boundary — set fetchedAt to exactly 5min ago, verify refresh is triggered. (2) Concurrent Report calls — launch 10 goroutines calling ReportMetrics simultaneously, verify no data races (run with -race), verify SecretFetcher is called at most once for initial resolution. (3) Stale fallback under repeated failures — fetch fails 3 times with stale cache, verify stale token is used each time and warning logged each time. (4) Token never appears in log output — use capturingHandler to capture all log records, verify none contain the test token string. (5) Empty batch handling — verify LocalReporter still makes the POST (consistent with platform reporter behavior).

tasks.title: HTTP edge case tests: TLS skip verify, request timeout, large batch (REQ-007, REQ-009)
tasks.description: Add edge case tests to `internal/metrics/local_reporter_test.go`: (1) TLS skip verify — create httptest.NewTLSServer, connect with TLSInsecureSkipVerify=true, verify success. Connect with TLSInsecureSkipVerify=false, verify TLS error. (2) Request timeout — create test server that sleeps 15s, verify LocalReporter returns timeout error within ~10s. (3) Large batch — create batch with 1000 MetricPoints, verify all are serialized and sent correctly. (4) Server closes connection mid-response — verify error is returned cleanly.

tasks.description: Create or extend documentation in the docs/ directory covering the LocalReporter and MultiReporter architecture. Reference doc should include: (1) LocalReporter: purpose, constructor parameters, HTTP behavior (POST, JSON, bearer auth), credential resolution flow (SecretFetcher → DecryptSecret → cache), TTL caching semantics, TLS configuration. (2) MultiReporter: purpose, parallel dispatch pattern, error isolation semantics (platform error returned, local error logged), constructor parameters. implementation_notes:
**Architecture**: Each pipeline (metrics, logfwd, auditfwd) gets its own LocalReporter and MultiReporter in its own package, following the codebase's self-contained package convention. The code structure is intentionally duplicated across packages rather than extracted into a shared package, because: (1) each pipeline has a different reporter interface, (2) the codebase favors narrow, focused packages over shared utility packages, (3) the duplication is small (~100 lines per LocalReporter, ~40 lines per MultiReporter).

**Credential Resolution Flow**: LocalReporter.resolveToken() checks cache (sync.RWMutex protected). If cache is valid (token non-empty and fetchedAt within 5min TTL), returns cached token. Otherwise calls SecretFetcher.FetchSecret(ctx, nodeID, cfg.SecretKey) to get SecretResponse, then DecryptSecret(nsk, resp.Ciphertext, resp.Nonce) to get plaintext. On success, updates cache. On failure with existing stale cache, logs warning and returns stale token. On failure with no cache, returns error.

**SecretFetcher Interface**: Defined per-pipeline (not shared) to match the codebase's pattern of defining interfaces where they're consumed. The interface matches nodeapi.SecretFetcher but is defined independently. The ControlPlane client satisfies this interface.

**HTTP Client**: Each LocalReporter creates its own http.Client in the constructor with: TLSClientConfig from LocalEndpointConfig.TLSInsecureSkipVerify, Timeout of 10 seconds. This is separate from the ControlPlane client's http.Client.

**MultiReporter Error Semantics**: The MultiReporter returns only the platform reporter's error. This is critical because the pipeline manager (Manager/Forwarder) uses the error to decide whether to retain the batch in the buffer for retry. Local endpoint errors should not trigger batch retention.

**Wiring Pattern in up.go**: For each pipeline, before the manager constructor call, add: `var metricsReporter metrics.MetricsReporter = client` then `if cfg.Metrics.LocalEndpoint.URL != "" { localReporter := metrics.NewLocalReporter(...); metricsReporter = metrics.NewMultiReporter(client, localReporter, logger) }` then pass `metricsReporter` to `metrics.NewManager()`.

**Key Files to Follow**: internal/api/endpoints.go (ControlPlane reporter pattern), internal/api/client.go (HTTP client construction pattern), internal/nodeapi/decrypt.go (DecryptSecret), internal/nodeapi/handler.go (SecretFetcher interface), internal/metrics/manager.go (MetricsReporter interface), internal/logfwd/source.go (LogReporter interface), internal/auditfwd/source.go (AuditReporter interface), internal/metrics/mock_manager_test.go (mock reporter test pattern), internal/api/types.go (batch types and LocalEndpointConfig).

**Potential Pitfalls**: (1) The NSK is identity.NodeSecretKey as string, must be converted to []byte for DecryptSecret. (2) The ControlPlane client's FetchSecret takes (ctx, nodeID, key) - nodeID must be passed correctly. (3) json.Marshal of batch types uses type aliases (MetricBatch = []MetricPoint) so marshaling works directly. (4) AuditEntry.Subject and Object are json.RawMessage - ensure they survive marshal/unmarshal round-trip. (5) The HTTP POST should not use gzip compression (unlike ControlPlane client) to keep LocalReporter simple.
